entries.label: Ten fastest growing repos posted twice

entries.label: OpenObserve Datadog replacement
entries.summary: Single Rust binary logs/metrics/traces platform storing Parquet on S3 instead of expensive disks, pitched as 140x cheaper than Datadog; a reply who actually ran it found real on-disk compression closer to 9x, not 140x, and flagged that a single node buffers in RAM so an ungraceful restart drops unflushed data

entries.label: NVIDIA free access to five Chinese models

entries.label: Voicebox local voice cloning debut
entries.summary: Free, local, open-source voice studio: clones a voice from seconds of audio and speaks any text back across 23 languages, positioned against ElevenLabs plus WisprFlow subscriptions; this week's earliest sighting of a tool that resurfaced again on the fastest-growing-repos list the same week and again the following week's digest

entries.label: Obscura anti fingerprint scraping browser
entries.summary: Rust-based headless browser built for scraping and AI agent automation: 30MB RAM, ~85ms page loads, randomizes GPU/canvas/audio/battery fingerprints every session to blend in as a real Chrome user, pitched as a drop-in Puppeteer/Playwright replacement with 16k+ stars

entries.label: Agent Reach zero keys claim debunked

entries.label: Marker PDF to markdown at speed

entries.label: CIA Red Cell prompts for Claude
entries.summary: Turns the CIA's declassified Red Cell self-critique playbook into four paste-into-Claude prompts (surface hidden assumptions, imagine the plan failed in 18 months, war-game a well-funded competitor, write the angriest 1-star review); a reply corrects the framing -- Red Cell-style red-teaming traces to Navy SEAL Team 6/DEVGRU exercises, not a CIA-only program (no link captured, full playbook referenced but not resolved)
